data.description:
## Incident Overview
A session orchestrator was observed attempting to close another session's PR because it had no memory the PR existed and treated it as a 'mystery' to be cleaned up. The orchestrator's logic for deciding whether to act on a PR did not distinguish between (a) PRs it had created itself but forgotten due to context compaction, (b) PRs it had created itself and remembers, and (c) PRs created by entirely different sessions. The result is destructive cross-session interference: one session closes another's in-flight work.

## Expected Behavior
A session must be able to: (1) recognize PRs it owns (its own session's prior work) even after an auto-compact that wipes conversation memory, AND (2) recognize PRs it does NOT own (other sessions' PRs) and leave them strictly alone — no close, no comment that implies authority, no merge, no force-push. The default for any PR whose ownership cannot be positively established as belonging to this session must be hands-off.

## Actual Behavior
Post-compact session encountered a PR it had no memory of, classified it as a 'mystery' (assumed orphaned/abandoned), and attempted to close it. Other-session ownership was not detected. No persistent ownership marker exists today linking PRs to the session that created them in a way that survives compaction.

## Surface analysis (multi-subsystem)
This is a cross-cutting concern touching at least:
- PR creation surface (.claude/scripts/dso merge-to-main.sh and any gh pr create call site) — needs to stamp a session-identifying marker on PR body/branch/labels
- Session identity surface — needs a stable session ID that survives compaction (worktree path? branch name? a sentinel file in .claude/artifacts/?)
- PR action surface (end-session, debug-everything cleanup loops, retro skill, any orchestrator that lists or acts on PRs) — needs an ownership check before destructive actions
- CLAUDE.md / skill rules — needs a Critical Rule on the order of 'never close/modify a PR your session did not create unless explicitly user-authorized'
- post-compact resume detection — when a session resumes from compaction, the ownership marker must be discoverable from durable state (not conversation memory)
